page: Microsoft Azure E2ns_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 vCPUs sourced from a single physical core with two threads on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Cache configuration includes 48 KB of L1d, 2 MB of L2, and 260 MB of L3 cache, backed by instruction set extensions including AVX-512, Intel AMX (tile and int8), and VAES. The configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not feature local storage disks or bundled GPUs, requiring remote storage volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark measurements reflect the constraints and capabilities of a single-core, dual-threaded architecture. In stress-ng evaluations, the single-core CPU throughput registers at 1664.89, whereas multi-core scaling yields 1703.0. Measured memory bandwidth reaches 133.07 GB/sec on cached 16 KB read blocks, scaling down to 16.17 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 11.56 GB/sec for 256 MB writes. Compression testing demonstrates 26.46 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 11.55 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. PassMark CPU and memory scores measure 3198.66 and 1562.78 respectively, accompanied by 2.35 million Redis SET operations per second and 3.73 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

The 1:8 core-to-memory ratio provides significant memory density relative to available CPU resources. However, high-throughput compute tasks are limited by the single physical core allocation, and disk operations depend on network-attached storage performance. This hardware balance aligns with small in-memory caching layers, low-concurrency relational databases, staging environments, and memory-dependent microservices that do not demand extensive multi-threaded compute capability.
